newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Enel full sell-off seen distant.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Enel full sell-off seen distant.

text.p: Italian state-owned electricity generator and distributor Enel is unlikely to be privatised fully in the next two years although the state might sell a stake of 10-20 percent, Enel's managing director was quoted as saying on Friday.

Franco Tato, Enel managing director, was quoted in Il Sole financial daily as saying the company would be happy if 20 percent were put on the stock market as experience showed even that amount of private investor weight reduced "political interference."
"I believe privatisation will not arrive during my mandate," Tato was quoted as telling a trade union seminar. His mandate runs to June 1999.
"Privatisation means that the state no longer has control. Maybe the Treasury will be able to place a minority stake of 10 to 20 percent," he added.
